AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How can compost be used in a garden? (1 mark)
   A. Feed it to fish
   B. Throw it away
   C. Mix it in planting holes or spread it around crops
   D. Use it to build a wall

2. Why should broken glass be kept out of compost? (1 mark)
   A. It rots too fast
   B. It does not rot and can cut people
   C. It makes the heap too wet
   D. It smells bad

3. How can you tell that a plant has enough water? (1 mark)
   A. The soil is dust
   B. The pot is empty
   C. The soil is damp about a finger deep
   D. The leaves are gone

4. What is a fuel? (1 mark)
   A. A cleaning tool
   B. A kind of food
   C. A type of soil
   D. Something we burn to get heat

5. What is biodiversity? (1 mark)
   A. The variety of living things on Earth
   B. A type of crop
   C. Only wild plants
   D. Only birds

6. How deep should tiny seeds be sown? (1 mark)
   A. On top of a heap
   B. About 30 cm
   C. As deep as a hand
   D. About 1 cm

7. What is a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. A type of crop
   B. A tool for digging
   C. The piece of ground prepared for sowing seeds
   D. A bed for sleeping

8. Why is dry grass laid lightly over a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. It makes seeds fly
   B. It makes the soil hard
   C. It keeps moisture and protects seeds from rain and birds
   D. It stops seeds growing

9. What is direct sowing? (1 mark)
   A. Buying young plants
   B. Watering seeds
   C. Sowing seeds where the crop will grow until harvest
   D. Sowing in a nursery

10. How fine should the soil in the seedbed be? (1 mark)
   A. Crumbly like brown sugar
   B. Hard like stone
   C. Full of big clods
   D. Wet like mud

11. What is a seedling? (1 mark)
   A. A dry stick
   B. A young plant grown from a seed
   C. A ripe fruit
   D. A type of soil

12. How far apart may passion fruit plants be planted? (1 mark)
   A. 30 metres
   B. 10 cm
   C. Touching
   D. About 2 to 3 metres

13. Which of these is a climbing fruit crop? (1 mark)
   A. Mango
   B. Guava
   C. Orange
   D. Passion fruit

14. What should be done with extra fruits? (1 mark)
   A. Bury them
   B. Leave them to rot
   C. Share or sell them and avoid wasting
   D. Throw them away

15. What is pruning? (1 mark)
   A. Watering the plant
   B. Cutting off dead, weak or unwanted branches
   C. Planting a seed
   D. Harvesting fruit

16. About how big should a planting hole for a fruit tree be? (1 mark)
   A. As big as a football field
   B. About 1 cm
   C. 10 cm wide only
   D. About half a metre wide and deep

17. How should the seedling be removed from its polythene bag? (1 mark)
   A. By pulling the stem hard
   B. By throwing it
   C. By cutting the roots
   D. Carefully so the ball of soil around roots does not break

18. Which product does a dairy cow give? (1 mark)
   A. Feathers
   B. Wool
   C. Milk
   D. Eggs

19. What is a male sheep called? (1 mark)
   A. Cock
   B. Ram
   C. Bull
   D. Billy

20. Which local vegetable is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Managu
   B. Rice
   C. Butter
   D. Ugali

21. Why is a meal of only chips not balanced? (1 mark)
   A. It lacks body-building and protective foods
   B. It has too many vegetables
   C. It has too much protein
   D. It has no energy

22. What should you hold hot pots with? (1 mark)
   A. Paper
   B. A wet cloth
   C. Bare hands
   D. A dry cloth or oven gloves

23. Which way should pot handles point? (1 mark)
   A. Outward over the floor
   B. Down into the fire
   C. Inward, away from the edge
   D. Towards children

24. What should be done with a fire after cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Add more wood
   B. Leave it burning
   C. Cover it with paper
   D. Put it out or switch off the gas

25. Which of these is used for shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. A bowl
   B. A frying pan
   C. A bucket
   D. A cup

26. What can be used if there is no soap? (1 mark)
   A. Mud
   B. Sugar
   C. Clean ash and running water
   D. Oil

27. Why is a tippy tap useful? (1 mark)
   A. It works without a water tap and saves water
   B. It needs electricity
   C. It cleans clothes
   D. It makes soap

28. How does the tippy tap release water? (1 mark)
   A. By a switch
   B. By a battery
   C. By a magnet
   D. A foot lever tips the container

29. What are germs? (1 mark)
   A. Types of food
   B. Large animals
   C. Kinds of soap
   D. Tiny living things that can cause disease

30. In which direction do you sweep a room? (1 mark)
   A. Only along the walls
   B. Only the middle
   C. Randomly
   D. From the corners towards the middle or door

31. Which method uses water and a mop? (1 mark)
   A. Burning
   B. Dusting
   C. Mopping
   D. Sweeping

32. What should you wear when handling rubbish? (1 mark)
   A. Gloves
   B. Only a hat
   C. Nothing
   D. Sandals only

33. Which PPE protects the feet from mud and water? (1 mark)
   A. Headgear
   B. Dust mask
   C. Gloves
   D. Gumboots

34. What should you do with cleaning materials afterwards? (1 mark)
   A. Give to animals
   B. Store them away from small children
   C. Drink them
   D. Leave them on the floor

35. Why should PPE be cleaned? (1 mark)
   A. To make it smell
   B. Dirty PPE can carry germs
   C. Dirty PPE lasts longer
   D. Clean PPE is heavier

36. How should rubber gloves be cleaned? (1 mark)
   A. Wash them with soap and water while wearing them, then rinse and hang to dry
   B. Wash with a stone
   C. Throw them in a fire
   D. Leave them dirty

37. What is the use of labelling PPE? (1 mark)
   A. To make it heavier
   B. To hide it
   C. So each item goes back to its owner
   D. To tear it

38. What is a hem? (1 mark)
   A. A needle
   B. A button
   C. A folded and stitched edge of cloth
   D. A hole

39. When is even tacking most useful? (1 mark)
   A. When you do not want to sew
   B. For curves and slippery cloth
   C. Only for paper
   D. Only for straight seams that need no hold

40. How should you finish a line of tacking? (1 mark)
   A. With scissors
   B. With a very big knot
   C. By pulling the thread out
   D. With a small back stitch

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Why should plastic not be burnt? (2 marks)

42. Explain the difference between variety and proportion in a meal. (3 marks)

43. Explain how to look after a compost heap for two months. (4 marks)

44. Write the steps for preparing a meal using both boiling and shallow frying. Include hygiene and safety. (5 marks)

45. Describe how to shallow fry an egg. (4 marks)

46. Give three peaceful ways of protecting crops from birds and animals apart from a scarecrow. (3 marks)

47. Explain the difference between domestic and wild animals. (2 marks)

48. Describe how to keep a food journal for one week. (4 marks)

49. Describe how to prepare a fine seedbed in three steps. (3 marks)

50. Why is poison or a trap not a good way of dealing with wild animals? (4 marks)

51. Name two other ways of saving water in the garden. (2 marks)

52. Write a plan for growing a passion fruit plant from planting to harvest. (5 marks)

53. Explain four ways germs can enter the body. (4 marks)

54. Explain four things that may happen to a child who does not eat a balanced diet. (4 marks)

55. Why should vegetables not be boiled for a long time? (3 marks)

56. Explain how domestic animals contribute to food production in a community. (5 marks)

57. Explain how animals help crops grow. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Mix it in planting holes or spread it around crops
   Compost feeds crops and improves the soil.

2. B — It does not rot and can cut people
   Glass never rots and can injure anyone handling the compost.

3. C — The soil is damp about a finger deep
   Feeling the soil shows if the roots have water.

4. D — Something we burn to get heat
   Fuels such as wood and gas are burnt for heat.

5. A — The variety of living things on Earth
   Biodiversity includes all the different animals and plants.

6. D — About 1 cm
   The smaller the seed, the shallower it should be sown.

7. C — The piece of ground prepared for sowing seeds
   A seedbed is where seeds are sown.

8. C — It keeps moisture and protects seeds from rain and birds
   Mulch protects the surface.

9. C — Sowing seeds where the crop will grow until harvest
   The seedlings are never moved.

10. A — Crumbly like brown sugar
   Fine crumbly soil lets seeds come up easily.

11. B — A young plant grown from a seed
   A seedling is a young plant.

12. D — About 2 to 3 metres
   Give climbers room.

13. D — Passion fruit
   Passion fruit needs support to climb.

14. C — Share or sell them and avoid wasting
   Extra fruits can earn money or feed others.

15. B — Cutting off dead, weak or unwanted branches
   Pruning helps light and air reach the plant.

16. D — About half a metre wide and deep
   The hole gives roots space in loose soil.

17. D — Carefully so the ball of soil around roots does not break
   Broken roots harm the seedling.

18. C — Milk
   Dairy cows are kept for milk.

19. B — Ram
   A ram is a male sheep.

20. A — Managu
   Managu is a green leafy vegetable.

21. A — It lacks body-building and protective foods
   Chips give mainly energy.

22. D — A dry cloth or oven gloves
   Wet cloth lets heat through.

23. C — Inward, away from the edge
   Handles sticking out can be knocked.

24. D — Put it out or switch off the gas
   This prevents accidents and saves fuel.

25. B — A frying pan
   A flat pan holds a little oil.

26. C — Clean ash and running water
   Ash helps to remove dirt when soap is not available.

27. A — It works without a water tap and saves water
   It can be made from a jerrican.

28. D — A foot lever tips the container
   Pushing the lever tips the container.

29. D — Tiny living things that can cause disease
   Germs cannot be seen without a microscope.

30. D — From the corners towards the middle or door
   This gathers dirt in one place.

31. C — Mopping
   Mopping washes floors.

32. A — Gloves
   Gloves protect from germs and cuts.

33. D — Gumboots
   Gumboots are waterproof.

34. B — Store them away from small children
   Keep them safe.

35. B — Dirty PPE can carry germs
   Clean PPE is safe and lasts longer.

36. A — Wash them with soap and water while wearing them, then rinse and hang to dry
   Washing with gloves on avoids touching dirt.

37. C — So each item goes back to its owner
   Labels avoid mix-ups.

38. C — A folded and stitched edge of cloth
   A hem stops edges fraying.

39. B — For curves and slippery cloth
   Even tacking holds firmly.

40. D — With a small back stitch
   Tacking must be easy to remove.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: The smoke is harmful to health and the environment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for harmful smoke, 1 mark for the environment or health.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Variety is eating many kinds of food; proportion is eating the right amount of each kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for variety, 1 mark for proportion, 1 mark for an example.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Keep it damp like a squeezed sponge, keep it covered, turn it after two to three weeks, and keep children and animals away.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct care activity, up to 4.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wash hands; wash food; boil potatoes until soft; shallow fry an egg or fish; serve with vegetables; safety: adult present, handles inward, dry cloth, water away from hot oil; clean up after.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for hygiene, 1 for boiling, 1 for frying, 1 for safety, 1 for serving and cleaning.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Crack the egg into a bowl; heat a little oil in the pan; slide the egg in; cook until the white is firm; lift out with a spatula.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Nets, fences, noise makers, shiny objects, guarding at the time animals come (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each method.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Domestic animals are kept and cared for by people. Wild animals live freely in nature.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw a table; write what you eat at every meal; write the group of each food; at the end of the week check which groups were missing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear weeds and stones; dig and loosen the soil; break the lumps with a rake until fine and level (add compost).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: It can kill other animals, pets and people, it hurts animals, and it harms nature.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason, up to 4.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mulching, collecting rainwater, watering in the morning or evening, reusing wash water (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

52. (5 marks)
   Answer: Build a trellis; dig and prepare a hole with compost; plant a seedling; water and mulch; tie the stem to the support; weed and prune; harvest ripe fruits and wash before eating.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage, up to 5.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Through the mouth from dirty hands, dirty food, dirty water, and through cuts or feet without shoes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: Weakness, tiredness, frequent illness, slow growth, poor concentration (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Long boiling removes vitamins into the water, so they lose their goodness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

56. (5 marks)
   Answer: They give milk, eggs and meat directly; their manure and draught power help to grow crops; and money from sales can buy other foods.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for direct food, 2 for crops, 1 for income.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: Their dung is used as manure, which feeds the soil, and oxen can be used to plough. Crops then grow well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for manure, 1 for ploughing, 1 for better crops.
